structure: Part 1 of 1, the whole ruling: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-06.md read in full, all 117 lines. Ian's ruling of 6 November 2026 on transporter management, lifting the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left pending requirements. Layout: a preamble (lines 1-26) naming the blocked question and quoting the owner in six blockquotes - four on who manages transporters, the mid-journey pattern and approved transporters (lines 7-16), then under a second lead-in two quoting the questions put back to the owner about the data model, the collection, roles and how Northern Ireland is held (lines 20-25); "## Decided" (lines 27-80) with six numbered points each marked "New." (address book as system of record; the mid-journey hand-off; approved transporters parked, with a further verbatim quote from later the same day on the eight shipped records and the increment movements that follow; the transporter as its own document in its own transporters collection; no roles but a private-or-commercial type; a commercial transporter's country forced to XI with no reference-data lookup); "## Follows from the decision, for the re-distil to work through" (lines 82-105) with five consequences 7 to 11 that the file says are not separate rulings but what the decisions mean for code already on main; "## Still open" (lines 107-110) with point 12; "## Unchanged" (lines 112-117) with point 13 on the Northern Ireland address search. Covered: every blockquote, every numbered point and sub-clause, the two question quotes recorded as questions rather than decisions, each point 7 to 11 claimed for what it states about today's code and what it leaves to the re-distil, point 12 and the re-distil hand-offs recorded as gap claims, plus five further gap claims for open points the ruling touches without settling.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.
claims.note: the owner says "may be", so the MDM management of the approved list is floated rather than settled here; decided point 3 parks it

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.
claims.quote: Don't worry about the approved transporters for now.

claims.statement: Whether transporters take the same data model as addresses, whether they can live in the address book service in a different collection, and whether they need the same roles, were put to the owner as questions rather than settled in his own words; the Decided points answer them.
claims.quote: So for question 1, the transporters don't need to be in the same data model as the addresses, but can live within the address book service if that makes sense? Persisted in a different collection? Would these transporters need the same roles?
claims.note: a question, not a decision: the decisions on these points are claimed from Decided points 4 and 5, never from this wording

claims.statement: Whether MDM is used for a Northern Ireland country lookup, or a created commercial transporter is simply forced to a Northern Ireland country code, was put to the owner as a question rather than settled in his own words; Decided point 6 answers it.
claims.quote: for the Northern Ireland thing, we wouldn't use MDM for a country look up right? We would just force a created commercial transporter to have a country code of northern Ireland?
claims.note: a question, not a decision: the decision is claimed from Decided point 6

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters: a transporter is a record held per organisation, exactly as every other address is.
claims.quote: **The address book manages transporters.** A transporter is a record held per organisation, exactly as every other address is, and `trade-imports-address-book` is the system of record.

claims.statement: trade-imports-address-book is the system of record for transporters.
claims.quote: `trade-imports-address-book` is the system of record

claims.statement: Decision 1 supersedes ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 and claim c-285.
claims.quote: This supersedes `ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5 and claim c-285

claims.statement: Decision 1 settles for transporters the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-093 left to "follow the real services".
claims.quote: and settles for transporters the question `ruling:sam-2026-10-09` p1-093 left to "follow the real services". New.

claims.statement: A notification journey that needs a new transporter opens the INS front door's add pages in journey mode and lands back in the journey on save or cancel.
claims.quote: A notification journey that needs a new transporter opens the INS front door's add pages in journey mode and lands back in the journey on save or cancel

claims.statement: Adding a transporter mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses - the same pattern as inc-077, inc-078 and inc-080 (EUDPA-706, merged e1237ac7) - and not a second pattern of its own.
claims.quote: **Adding a transporter mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses.** ... the same pattern as inc-077, inc-078 and inc-080 (EUDPA-706, merged `e1237ac7`), not a second pattern of its own. New.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are parked: a list of approved transporters managed in MDM for every organisation, added on top of an organisation's own transporters, is not in scope now and nothing is built for it.
claims.quote: **Approved transporters are parked.** A list of approved transporters managed in MDM for every organisation, added on top of an organisation's own transporters, is not in scope now and nothing is built for it.

claims.statement: The approved-transporters list is recorded as the likely subject of the 9 October block.
claims.quote: It is recorded as the likely subject of the 9 October block. New.
claims.note: the ruling says "likely", so it records a reading of the earlier block rather than a certainty

claims.statement: The eight transporter records the service ships to every organisation are the approved transporters in an initial hardcoded form, and they are parked with the rest.
claims.quote:
> yes the shipped transporters are the approved transporters in an initial hardcoded fashion, move them out into the other blocked increment

So the eight records `services/transporters/records.js` ships to every organisation **are** the approved transporters, in an initial hardcoded form, and they are parked with the rest.
claims.note: clarified later the same day, when the re-analysis asked whether the transporters the service ships are that concept

claims.statement: The two commercial placeholder transporter records on main are not replaced with Design Release 2.1's four.
claims.quote: They stay exactly as they are: main's two commercial placeholders are not replaced with Design Release 2.1's four

claims.statement: The shipped private transporter records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed.
claims.quote: and the private records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed.

claims.statement: Design Release 2.1's transporter records (req-397, req-398) and picking one of the eight shipped records moved off inc-037 to inc-265, with the list question (req-2172).
claims.quote: Design Release 2.1's records (req-397, req-398) and picking one of those eight moved off inc-037 to inc-265 with the list question (req-2172).

claims.statement: inc-037 still builds the transporter list over whatever the organisation itself has added, which the address book holds under decision 1.
claims.quote: What inc-037 still builds is the list over whatever the organisation itself has added, which the address book holds under decision 1.

claims.statement: A transporter is its own record in its own collection inside the address book service, and does not take the Address data model.
claims.quote: **A transporter is its own record in its own collection, inside the address book service.** It does not take the `Address` data model.

claims.statement: A transporter is persisted in a transporters collection beside addresses, with its own document, controller, repository and route.
claims.quote: It is persisted in a `transporters` collection beside `addresses`, with its own document, controller, repository and route

claims.statement: The transporter record reuses the address book service's organisation scoping (IdentityHeaderFilter), soft-delete status, optimistic locking and Standard Address Block field validation where the fields are genuinely the same.
claims.quote: reusing the service's organisation scoping (`IdentityHeaderFilter`), soft-delete status, optimistic locking and the Standard Address Block field validation where the fields are genuinely the same

claims.statement: The address book's own API is unchanged by the transporter work.
claims.quote: The address book's own API is unchanged

claims.statement: AddressRequest requires at least one role (@NotEmpty), which a transporter cannot satisfy.
claims.quote: `AddressRequest` requires at least one role (`@NotEmpty`) ... which a transporter can satisfy neither of

claims.statement: AddressRequest refuses a type outright (@Null, "type is not a supported field"), which a transporter cannot satisfy.
claims.quote: refuses a `type` outright (`@Null`, "type is not a supported field"), which a transporter can satisfy neither of

claims.quote: a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has. New.

claims.statement: A transporter carries a private-or-commercial type, which no address has.
claims.quote: a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has. New.

claims.statement: A transporter carries an approval status, which no address has.
claims.quote: a transporter carries an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status that no address has. New.

claims.quote: `AddressRole` exists to say which records a notification's picker may offer for a slot

claims.quote: and to drive the receiving-roles-in-the-United-Kingdom rule

claims.quote: and the list's three category tabs

claims.quote: A transporter is never one of those six roles and has one use — the transporter step — so a role would carry no information

claims.quote: and no seventh role or fourth role group is added

claims.quote: **Transporters have no roles. They have a type.** ... What is stored instead is the private-or-commercial type

claims.quote: which is intrinsic: it decides the form, the field list and the country rule, so unlike an address's type (which `ruling:paul-2026-11-05` dropped as derivable from roles) it cannot be derived from anything.

claims.statement: The INS front door's Transporter tab is a fourth tab backed by the transporters route, not a fourth role group over addresses.
claims.quote: The INS front door's Transporter tab is therefore a fourth tab backed by the transporters route, not a fourth role group over `addresses`. New.

claims.statement: A commercial transporter's country is forced to XI, with no reference-data lookup.
claims.quote: **A commercial transporter's country is forced to `XI`, with no reference-data lookup.**

claims.statement: A commercial transporter's country is not a choice: the add form fixes the country and posts it in a hidden field.
claims.quote: It is not a choice, so there is nothing to look up: the add form already fixes the country, posts it in a hidden field

claims.statement: The commercial transporter add form refuses a tampered country value rather than correcting it.
claims.quote: and refuses a tampered value rather than correcting it (c-055)

claims.quote: MDM could not serve it in any case — its country list is the origin and export list, 249 entries with no United Kingdom at all

claims.quote: which is why `addressCountries()` prepends `GB`/`United Kingdom` in code

claims.statement: The country code persisted for a commercial transporter is XI, displayed as "Northern Ireland".
claims.quote: The code persisted is `XI`, displayed as "Northern Ireland"

claims.statement: Both the XI code and its "Northern Ireland" display name are held as constants in the service.
claims.quote: both held as constants in the service

claims.statement: XI is this estate's existing code for Northern Ireland: trade-imports-schemas' DOCOM samples carry "countryId": "XI" with "countryName": "United Kingdom (Northern Ireland)" against Belfast BT postcodes.
claims.quote: `XI` is this estate's existing code for Northern Ireland: `trade-imports-schemas`' DOCOM samples carry `"countryId": "XI"` with `"countryName": "United Kingdom (Northern Ireland)"` against Belfast BT postcodes.

claims.statement: Because XI is distinct from GB, "must be Northern Ireland" stays enforceable from the stored value alone, with no postcode parsing and no extra flag.
claims.quote: Being distinct from `GB`, it keeps "must be Northern Ireland" enforceable from the stored value alone, with no postcode parsing and no extra flag

claims.quote: and it keeps a transporter's country the same type as the address book's `countryCode` rather than today's display string

claims.statement: A private transporter is unaffected by the XI rule and keeps its real choice of country from the United Kingdom plus reference-data's export countries.
claims.quote: A **private** transporter is unaffected and keeps its real choice of country from the United Kingdom plus reference-data's export countries (inc-008). New.

claims.statement: Points 7 to 11 are not separate rulings: they are what the six decisions mean for code already on main, and the re-distil of the transporter area should settle each against the real services.
claims.ref: ruling-ian-2026-11-06.md "Follows from the decision, for the re-distil to work through" lead-in, lines 82-85

claims.statement: The animals frontend's transporter store is not the system of record.
claims.quote: The animals frontend's transporter store is not the system of record.

claims.statement: Today the animals frontend keeps added transporters in an in-memory Map per process, so they are lost on restart.
claims.quote: `services/transporters/register.js` keeps added transporters in an in-memory `Map` per process, lost on restart and not shared between instances.

claims.statement: Today the animals frontend's added transporters are not shared between instances.
claims.quote: lost on restart and not shared between instances

claims.statement: Under decision 1 the address book replaces the animals frontend's in-memory transporter store.
claims.quote: Under decision 1 the address book replaces it.

claims.statement: inc-039's requirement that added transporters "stay on its list for later notifications" becomes real persistence rather than the current demo-grade capture.
claims.quote: inc-039's requirement that added transporters "stay on its list for later notifications" becomes real persistence rather than the current demo-grade capture.

claims.statement: The transporter add pages live in the INS front door beside the other address add pages, rather than in the animals frontend's features/transport/transporter-add, .../private-transporter-details and .../commercial-transporter-details.
claims.quote: The add pages' home follows decision 2: the INS front door, beside the other address add pages, rather than `features/transport/transporter-add`, `.../private-transporter-details` and `.../commercial-transporter-details` in the animals frontend.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what becomes of the animals frontend's three transporter add-page folders, handing it to the re-distil to decide against the real services.

claims.statement: inc-074, inc-075 and inc-076 become the primary route to adding a transporter rather than an extra one.
claims.quote: inc-074, inc-075 and inc-076 become the primary route rather than an extra one

claims.statement: The Transporter option on the "Choose an address type" page now has somewhere to lead.
claims.quote: and the Transporter option on "Choose an address type" now has somewhere to lead

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open which of two placements the Transporter option takes on "Choose an address type" - req-1198's third, before "Branch", or req-2042's after "Place of Destination" and before the divider - handing it to the re-distil to settle against the three-option page inc-061 built.
claims.quote: Which of the two placements still in play it takes — req-1198's third, before "Branch", or req-2042's after "Place of Destination" and before the divider — is settled at the re-distil against the three-option page inc-061 built.
claims.note: open point the ruling touches but does not settle; the two candidate placements are recorded here, not chosen

claims.statement: A transporter's approval status is Approved or New, and is shown on the transporter list.
claims.quote: A transporter's approval status (Approved or New, shown on the list)

claims.statement: A transporter's approval status is not the address book's AddressStatus, which is an ACTIVE or DELETED soft-delete tombstone.
claims.quote: is not the address book's `AddressStatus`, which is an ACTIVE or DELETED soft-delete tombstone.

claims.statement: Because decision 4 puts transporters and addresses on one service, the transporter document needs its own name for its approval-status concept.
claims.quote: Decision 4 puts the two on one service, so the transporter document needs its own name for its own concept.

claims.statement: Decision 6 makes a commercial transporter's stored country a code rather than today's display string 'Northern Ireland'.
claims.quote: Decision 6 makes the commercial transporter's stored country a code rather than today's display string `'Northern Ireland'`

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what happens to transporter records captured before the country-code change, if any outlive it, handing it to the re-distil to say.
claims.quote: so the re-distil should say what happens to records captured before the change, if any outlive it.
claims.note: open point the ruling touches but does not settle

claims.statement: Which approved-transporter list the transporter list's commercial records come from (req-2172, inc-265) stays open, parked with decision 3.
claims.quote: **Which approved-transporter list the list's commercial records come from** (req-2172, inc-265) stays open, parked with decision 3.
claims.note: the ruling records this as its one explicitly still-open point

claims.statement: The Northern Ireland address search (inc-042) stays blocked on its own, independent blocker, unchanged by this ruling.
claims.quote: The Northern Ireland address search (inc-042) stays blocked on its own, independent blocker

claims.statement: The INS address lookup is still only the EUDPA-390 spike, gated to dev and local and not wired in.
claims.quote: the INS address lookup is still only the EUDPA-390 spike, gated to dev and local and not wired in.

claims.statement: The Northern Ireland address search waits with the address book's own inc-072 and inc-081, which wait on the same thing.
claims.quote: It waits with the address book's own inc-072 and inc-081, which wait on the same thing.

claims.statement: Under decision 6 the Northern Ireland address search's BT-postcode filter is a search convenience, not the source of truth for the country.
claims.quote: Under decision 6 its BT-postcode filter is a search convenience, not the source of truth for the country.

claims.statement: The ruling names a transporter's approval status values (Approved, New) but does not say what sets a transporter to Approved, who may change the status, or whether an organisation's own added transporter starts as New.
claims.note: the ruling touches the approval status in two places without settling how it is set

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the transporter record's full field list is: it names an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status, and reuses Standard Address Block validation only "where the fields are genuinely the same", without saying which address block fields a transporter keeps or drops.

The ruling does not say what the transporters route's API surface is - the paths, whether a transporter can be edited or deleted, or whether the transporter list is paged - though it gives the transporter its own controller, repository and route and a soft-delete status.

The ruling does not say where the eight hardcoded shipped transporter records live while they are parked - whether they stay in the animals frontend's services/transporters/records.js or move to the address book under decision 1 - only that they stay exactly as they are and move to inc-265.

The ruling does not say whether the forced XI country is enforced by the address book service as well as by the add form: it names the add form's hidden field and refusal of a tampered value, and the constants held in the service, without saying which service validates a commercial transporter's country on write.
